character.name: Sebak
character.title: The Crow in the Wind
character.lineage: Half-Uchiha (Son of Uchiha Itachi) / Unknown Maternal Bloodline

alar.notes: 1 firm Alar binding in combat (scales with Intelligence and University training)

weapons.name: Twine bolas (2 kunai)
weapons.properties: Thrown (15/30 ft), improvised, no proficiency; a hit restrains the target until it uses an action to free itself, Strength check DC 11; two kunai are tied up in it

features.name: Improved Flicker (Body Flicker)
features.description: Teleport/dash up to 30 ft. to an unoccupied space you can see without provoking opportunity attacks. Improved at Rogue 2 (in place of Cunning Action): you can Hide as part of the same bonus action, with advantage on the Stealth check if the destination offers cover, dim light or breaks line of sight; and anyone relying on sight to see where you went has disadvantage on Perception checks to spot your new position. Costs no extra action or chakra.

features.name: Chakra-Fuelled Link
features.description: Act as a pure, lossless thermal/kinetic source for a Sympathetic binding for 1 round, bypassing the need for a fire or the risk of Binder's Chills.

features.name: Precision Throw
features.description: Curve a thrown kunai/dagger around half or three-quarters cover, granting Advantage on the attack roll.

features.name: Setting a Binding
features.description: Bonus action to set up, whatever the link quality. Roll an Alar check: d20 + INT + proficiency, plus WIS when focused (lost if you took damage or were grappled since your last turn; advantage after a calm round of preparation). DC by link: Perfect 8, Good 11, Poor 15. A failure means slippage and a partial effect, not a miss. A binding acting on a person lets them save against your Sympathy DC. Maintaining it is free but occupies your one mental split. Shares your bonus action with Body Flicker.

features.name: Link Efficiency
features.description: Perfect Link (same piece of matter): DC 8, ~80-90%. Good Link (similar material, or blood/hair for organic targets): DC 11, ~40-60%. Poor Link (crude similarity): DC 15, ~5-15%, high slippage.

features.name: Binder's Chills
features.description: Drawing heat from your own body requires a CON save (DC 10 + energy level) or take 1d4 cold damage and 1 level of Exhaustion.

features.name: Sneak Attack (1d6)
features.description: Extra 1d6 damage when hitting with a Finesse/Ranged weapon with Advantage, or when an ally (or an active Sympathetic kinetic binding distracting the target) is within 5 ft. of the enemy.

features.name: Uchiha Dormancy (Sharingan)
features.description: The Sharingan is locked. Extreme emotional trauma or life-or-death catalysis may awaken it.

features.name: Unknown Maternal Bloodline
features.description: Passive triggers observed by the DM during high-stress physical or sympathetic events. Surrounding matter hums and vibrates. Stirred at the brink of death at the felled oak: iron and wood within reach rang and the nearest club shattered. It drained his chakra and left him exhausted. Its nature is still unknown.

features.name: Counterweight
features.description: Learned from Ashdown. When you set a binding on a Poor link, balance it against a second object of similar mass: treat the link as Good (DC 11) for that binding. The second object must be in the binding and is part of the sympathy.

items.name: Hemp rope (20 ft)
items.notes: Used to tie Pell; cut from the beam, now with Voss or in the loft

items.name: Watch receipt for a light crossbow and 7 bolts
items.notes: Held a month at the south gate by Sergeant Voss; the crossbowman's, taken in defence of the cart

items.name: Bram's note for Rennick
items.notes: Folded twice, sealed with Bram's thumbprint in ink; says the bearer carries his box and his word and is to be paid what is due

items.name: Marta's note for Corwin Hale
items.notes: Introduces Sebak to Corwin Hale, a journeyman of the Medica at the University; asks him to spare a quarter of an hour

items.name: Voss's signed note
items.notes: Says the strongbox was inspected sealed, locked and whole at the south gate at first light on Wednesday. H. Voss, Sergeant of the Watch, with his thumbprint

items.name: Voss's receipt for the strongbox
items.notes: One iron-bound strongbox, sealed, received at the south gate on Wednesday morning and held unopened by the watch

items.name: Counting-house paper No. 417 (register name: Crow)
items.notes: Cealdish counting-house on Lamplight Street, clerk Ostrel. Whoever holds this paper may collect the strongbox, the satchel of six pale bars and a sealed pouch with the iron key. Paid one jot for the night of Wednesday

items.name: Iron-bound strongbox
items.notes: Heavy; seal lifted and replaced; holds six wrapped river stones, not the bars

items.name: Nightsilver shaving
items.notes: Bound to the five bars Sebak handed to Ashdown: a Perfect link that tracks their motion and direction (occupies his mental split)

items.name: Nightsilver bar
items.notes: Payment from Ashdown. Nightsilver stores energy and relays a binding with almost no slippage; never heat it fast (it flares white)

items.name: Black felt hat (Uchiha fan)
items.notes: Meris dyed it black and stitched a small red-and-white round fan on the left of the band, the Uchiha crest as Sebak described it; keeps the rain off and the face in shadow

keepsakes: Small wooden amulet containing a single black crow feather (mother's warning)

world.location: The Ferry-Pole inn, where the river path meets the east road
world.weather: Cold and grey, mist off the river

companions.name: Tamsin
companions.notes: Young, earnest University hopeful with a lame mule named Biscuit. Knows book sympathy (chalk circles) but is clumsy at it. Sebak has agreed to walk with him as far as the University gates.

enemies.name: Masked intruder
enemies.notes: Knocked out with a pommel strike; wakes with 1 HP in about an hour, or sooner with smelling salts or cold water. Face still wrapped.

last_log: Sebak and Tamsin take rooms at the Ferry-Pole inn for the night.
notes:
COSTINGS (GM reference, using the player's table of the Cealdish system). 10 drabs = 1 jot, 10 jots = 1 talent (100 drabs), 10 talents = 1 mark. Below the drab is the shim (an iron scrap by weight, ~11-14 to a drab). Compound prices like 'two and four' mean talents and jots. Benchmarks: 1 drab = casual stake, 3-4 drabs = a big meal, 5 drabs = road provisions at an Imre inn. 1 jot = Eolian cover or work aprons; 1-2 jots = a student's weekly wage; 2 jots = wagon passage; 3 jots = a sturdy second-hand cloak. 1 talent = a University term's room and board, or good shoes. 2-3 talents = average tuition. 8-10 talents = a quality steel crossbow or a master lute. Price new things in drabs and jots by default. PRICES RESET (the player agreed to a fair readjustment): barge-guard day job = 2 jots + board. Apothecary in Imre = 3 jots for the first treatment (she returned 7 jots of the talent Sebak paid, saying Sebak's field stitching saved her work), then 5 drabs/day for bed and physic, hay 2 drabs/day. Bram's promised pay for the road to Imre = a few jots wage plus about a talent as a thank-you bonus if he recovers. Sebak's looted light crossbow is ordinary, not 'quality steel': about 2-3 talents to a buyer. The player wants tuition to stay hard to afford.

STORY THREADS: Bram's strongbox (small, iron-bound, locked, heavy, under the wagon bench) and the crossbowman's iron key (scar down left cheek, aimed at Bram, patient, likely hired). Whether the key fits the strongbox is undecided; do not confirm until the player asks Bram. Voss (south gate sergeant) is sending men for the bodies; the dead brigand may be Garrick Finch (missing front tooth, left forearm tattoo) with a bounty on the roll; the fled one is heavy-set, brown patched coat, broken nose, stubble, headed east, lost his club. Crossbow and 7 bolts held by Voss for a month on a receipt.

BRAM'S ACCOUNT (told to Sebak Tuesday evening): the strongbox is not his. A thin man in grey paid him half a talent up front at his Crosson stall nine days ago, the rest due on delivery to a factor called Rennick on Gilder's Row, Imre, into his hands only. Bram never opened it; heavy for its size, no clink, 'metal in cloth, or books'. The man in grey kept the key and said Rennick would have the other; Bram must deliver it locked. Sebak's wage rides on delivery. Bram does not yet know about the crossbowman's key. Who the man in grey is, what is in the box and whether Rennick is honest are undecided; Rennick, the box and the key are linked to the ambush.

MORE FROM BRAM: never met the man in grey before. He came to Bram's Crosson stall at close of market: thin, grey cloak, hood half up, gloves, soft clerkish voice, accent from east of the river. He knew Bram's name, his mule's name and his monthly Imre run, and asked for a 'discreet' commission. Paid half a talent in clean Cealdish silver, counted out himself. Asked if Bram would travel alone; Bram said he would hire a guard; the man said 'Do as you like.' Bram suspects he only wanted him on that road on that day. Unresolved: who the man in grey is and who recommended Bram.

SEBAK TAKES THE DELIVERY: Bram gave 4 jots now and a thumb-marked note for Rennick. Balance due from Rennick on delivery is 1.5 talents; Bram promises Sebak 1 talent of it. Box and wagon are in the livery yard behind the apothecary; the girl will unlock the bench in the morning. Not moved tonight.

TRAP TUESDAY NIGHT: Sebak cut a hand's length of wax-coated twine, one end knotted to the strongbox's iron handle, the same piece of twine so a Perfect link (DC 8); Alar check 21 (adv, 15 and 7). The intruder's pull is the kinetic source, so no chakra and no Binder's Chills. It occupies his one mental split all night; it holds through ordinary sleep, frays if he is knocked out or takes a hard blow. A tug wakes him instantly.

STRONGBOX SECRETS (GM only): the crossbowman's key FITS the lock. The lid seam has an obvious strip of grey paper under a blank grey wax disc (Sebak has seen it). HIDDEN: a hair is stretched across the seam under the paper (DC 12 to spot; Sebak rolled 10 and missed it); lifting the lid breaks it and Rennick or any careful inspector will see the box was opened. The key's fit means whoever sent the crossbowman could open the box after killing Bram. Contents still undecided (heavy, muffled, metal in cloth or books).

STRONGBOX OPENED Tuesday night (Sleight 24, seal lifted whole with lamp-chimney heat and laid on Sebak's knee; it can be pressed back on). The hidden hair under the paper was broken by lifting the lid and Sebak did not notice. CONTENTS: (1) thick ledger in grey leather, strap and brass clasp, columns of names, dates and sums in a cramped shorthand; (2) about a dozen small letters tied with black thread, no names or addresses; (3) six flat hand-length bars of dull, unmarked pale metal, each wrapped in cloth, lighter than steel, heavier than tin (undecided: assay, silver alloy, a sympathy-relevant metal?). Sebak has touched nothing but the oilcloth.

THE BARS: Sebak (Investigation 17) knows they are NOT silver, tin, lead, iron or common alloys: short dull note when tapped, hard (kunai barely scores), bright scratch that does not tarnish, chills slowly in the hand. He cannot name it. Truth still undecided; an assay at the University or a sympathist could name it. Value unknown (fortune or nothing).

BARS TESTED: Sebak dropped the twine alarm to test two bars (Good link DC 11, check 17, kinetic source only). The bars carry sympathy with almost no slippage, far better than iron: a sympathist's metal, likely very valuable to a sympathist or the University. The twine alarm is NOT set at present; Sebak must re-set it (Alar DC 8) if he wants it.

LETTERS (Investigation 10, gist only): addressed only to 'R.', signed with a drawn small square; loose shorthand, no names. They discuss a consignment (the 'grey', 'the weight'), sums matching the ledger. Buyer 'will name his own price when he has seen it'; the Arcanum's clerks must not hear; 'carters are being counted at the Omethi bridge', goods must move 'by a man nobody watches'. One reply in a firmer hand (R.): 'Send it sealed and send it whole. If it comes to me opened, I will not receive it, and I will not pay.' Sebak retied the threads in the same knots. Bram was chosen as an unwatched carrier. Whether Rennick = R. is likely but undecided. The hidden hair (broken) is the 'whole' check R. will make.

LEDGER (Investigation 10, partial): about twelve rows over a year or more; each: date, six (bars), a large sum, a symbol place-mark, a word. Most 'd.' (delivered), two 'lost, recovered', one 'lost'. Last row, newest, six bars and in different ink 'tinker' with a small tick (undecided: tick means expected, or means spent). Sebak could not tell what 'lost' means (bars, carriers, or both). Clasp has a faint thumbnail scratch.

SWAP: Sebak replaced the six bars with six river stones wrapped in oilcloth (weight check Investigation 11 vs DC 12: FAILED by 1, the box is a shade lighter than it was; an attentive carrier or Rennick may notice). Bars hidden under hay in the loft corner beneath the window. Seal re-pressed (Sleight 15 vs 13, OK). The hidden hair was never found or restored (still broken). Twine alarm re-set (Alar 18 vs DC 8), occupying his one mental split.

NIGHT INTRUDER (random night roll 4): slim figure, dark clothes, hood, cloth over lower face, rag-bound boots, shuttered lantern, thin pick or blade, found the seal. Entered by the ladder hatch without Sebak or the donkey noticing; the twine alarm woke Sebak. Intruder is ten feet away at the box, back half turned, unaware Sebak is awake. Identity undecided (a hired thief, not the fled brigand). Sebak has surprise if he acts first. Not yet an encounter; set encounter.active when blows begin.

FIGHT: Sebak at 6/10 HP after the intruder's hit (4). Twine alarm still held; Sebak took damage so his Alar has no WIS bonus until his next turn passes. Intruder unnamed, a competent burglar-blade (about 12 HP, AC 13, Acrobatics +5).

TWINE ALARM DROPPED for the burning binding (mental split now used by the blood-and-flame binding on the intruder). Burning cloak near the strongbox and the hay (fire hazard, Marta forbade open flame).

INTRUDER DOWN: nonlethal, unconscious until about an hour passes (or smelling salts / cold water). Search and unmask pending. Slim, hooded, rag-bound boots, short blade (on the floor), shuttered lantern, burned cloak. Marta is awake below and calling up. Fight over; the twine alarm is NOT set. Sebak 6/10 HP, chakra 2.

PELL (the burglar, about thirty, lean, shaven, nick in one ear) interrogated Wed small hours: hired by a heavy man with broken nose, stubble, patched brown coat, bandaged hand (the fled brigand), who paid a half-talent in Cealdish silver at the Salt Barrel (cheap smoky tavern by the wharf) 'last night' and said a locked box was in the apothecary's loft with a hired blade and a tinker sleeping near it. Pell's goods: lockpicks and pry-bar, purse with five silver jots (a half-talent), tin token stamped with a barrel (credit at the Salt Barrel). Marta sent her girl for Sergeant Voss (about a quarter of an hour). Pell knows nothing more. The brigand is in Imre, probably at or near the Salt Barrel.

PELL ON HOBB: Hobb mended locks in a back room off Tallow Lane and fenced goods; small, bald, bad chest; died two winters ago. Taught Pell. Pell read the strongbox's lock: Severen work, made for the box, not bought off a shelf (whoever commissioned it had money). Voss (or watchmen) are arriving in the yard now.

VOSS ARRIVED IN THE LOFT: took Pell (to the cells; hearing before the magistrate), pocketed Pell's purse as evidence, ordered a written account from Sebak and Marta by noon, will send two men to the Salt Barrel at first light, and says the strongbox must stay where it is until he has seen it himself, open or shut. Voss has NOT inspected the box yet. The box contains six wrapped river stones; the six bars are under the hay in the loft corner by the window; the seal was lifted and replaced; the hidden hair is broken; the weight is a little light. Danger point: Voss opening the box.

DEAL FOR PELL: Sebak argued for rehabilitation (Persuasion 18 vs DC 14). Voss will hold Pell one night in the cells; tomorrow Pell shows Voss's men the heavy broken-nosed man at the Salt Barrel and swears before the magistrate; then a year's service with the watch's locksmith (mending gaol doors, teaching the watch how thieves think) for bed, board and a drab a day. Back to thieving = stocks. Marta will stitch Sebak's ribs next.

Marta stitched Sebak (six stitches, poultice), no charge; counted as spending his Hit Die (1d8+2 = 7), now HP 10/10, no Hit Dice left. Told: no lifting for two days and no bindings that need running about (flavour). Marta has asked whether the box will bring more trouble to her door. Dawn is near; Voss wants a written account by noon and to see the box. Strongbox (with stones) and bars (under hay by the loft window) are unwatched in the loft; the twine alarm is not set.

ASSAY BY MARTA (2 jots): filed a pinch from one bar. Dense, near silver but not silver; aqua fortis barely marks it; does not tarnish; in a flame it does not melt or blacken and flares once with a cool white moonlike light. Not in her assay books. Marta advises showing it quietly to someone at the University. Marta knows only that there is an unnamed metal; she did not see the bars or the box contents. Sebak filed a pinch from one bar (a little missing). One bar's filings stay with Marta's paper.

CORWIN HALE: journeyman of the Medica (six years), crosses the Omethi every second week for willow bark and poppy, careful and honest by Marta's account. Marta knows no sympathists; the Arcanum doesn't visit her shop. Marta advises: tell Hale little, and do not go to the Arcanum first.

SEBAK LEAVES MARTA'S carrying the strongbox (stones) openly in both arms and the satchel of bars under his cloak, heading for the south gate to show Voss. Voss will see the box. Risk: Voss lifts or opens it and finds stones; the seal was re-pressed, the hidden hair is broken, the weight is a little light.

VOSS EXAMINED THE BOX (no break): he walked round it, lifted one corner an inch, ran a thumb along the paper strip. His Investigation roll (3+3 = 6 vs the reseal's 15) failed: he does not notice the seal was lifted, nor the broken hair, nor the stones. He did not open it ('I will not break another man's seal without cause'). He has not noticed the weight. He asked where Sebak is taking it. Voss has Pell in the cell behind him; his men are still on the road for the bodies.

VOSS'S NOTE: he deliberately wrote what he saw (sealed, whole) and added he did not open it; he suspects Sebak is hiding something but trusts him as straight so far. Sebak told Voss only that he would deliver the box to its 'intended target'. Voss does NOT know the name Rennick. Voss expects Sebak's written account at noon.

VOSS OFFERS HESK as a plain-clothes tail fifty paces behind Sebak (the younger, thin watchman who sneered at the crossbow). He would learn Rennick's name and Voss would know by noon. Sebak has not yet answered (accepts or goes alone). Voss will not force it.

BOX HELD BY VOSS: the strongbox is in the cupboard behind Voss's chair, locked, key on his belt, unopened. Sebak holds a receipt. Sebak goes to the Salt Barrel with Voss's men (Orrin, broad and sleepy; Hesk in plain brown coat; Pell in iron cuffs). Sebak told to keep his hood up and say nothing. Sebak still has the satchel of bars (unresolved where it goes). Voss was told nothing about the bars and did not ask.

AT THE SALT BARREL: about eight people (porters at a long table, a woman asleep in a corner, a thin man by the hearth, a barman who looked toward the back when the watch came in). The heavy brown-coated broken-nosed man with a bandaged hand sleeps on a bench at the cold end of the hearth, back corner. Pell signalled with a chin lift. Orrin takes the front, Hesk goes round the side wall, Sebak waits at the door with hood up. The barman may be warning the man or part of the ring (undecided). Sebak still has the satchel of bars under his cloak.

BRIGAND ARRESTED at the Salt Barrel (Orrin and Hesk); no fight. He is afraid not of the watch but of someone else; wants a locked door; says he will talk to anyone. Recognised Sebak as 'the quiet one from the road'. Name still unknown (the dead one may be Garrick Finch; the runner could be someone else). HIDDEN: Sebak failed Perception (9 vs 12): the barman slipped out the back door during the arrest (to warn the man in grey / a contact); the watch will notice the empty counter on leaving. Sebak still carries the bars.

CALDER MARSH (the heavy broken-nosed man) talked to Voss alone: hired in Imre a fortnight ago by a thin man in grey (gloves, soft voice, face never seen) for three talents: stop the tinker's wagon on the south road, the tinker 'not to arrive', the box brought back. The scarred crossbowman, VERRIN, was the grey man's own man and ran it; the key was Verrin's job. The grey man told them if the box reached its buyer they would all be sorry. Calder is more afraid of the grey man's other people than of the watch. Voss's men found the dead brigand, Garrick Finch, and NO crossbowman: Verrin woke and walked off (jot gone, blood on the roots, trail into the thicket). Verrin is loose. The barman at the Salt Barrel slipped out during the arrest (Hesk noticed afterwards). Sebak's account is due at noon.

VOSS: Sebak skipped the written account; Voss will write it himself from Sebak's spoken word and expects his thumb on it when he next passes. Voss took the strongbox out of the cupboard and put it on the table for Sebak to take (still unopened by him). He warns time matters: the barman likely tipped off the grey man's people; Verrin is loose. Hesk is again offered as a tail; Sebak has not decided.

STREET INCIDENT: a boy of eight to ten (grubby, big frightened eyes), paid a drab by a 'long grey coat' by the pie barrow to bump Sebak and look in his sack, tried to cut the satchel strap (Sleight 10 vs passive Perception 13, caught). Hesk holds the boy. The man in the long grey coat vanished. Someone is watching and knows Sebak carries something. Sebak accepted Hesk as a tail (50 paces behind, plain brown coat). Next: Gilder's Row, Rennick's house.

COUNTING-HOUSE (Lamplight Street, brass ship plate, two red-and-black Cealdish door guards): clerk OSTREL (neat, balding, black coat, soft Cealdish accent). A jot a night in advance, a numbered paper, the house holds sealed things untouched and releases only to the bearer of the paper. They do not ask what is inside and do not look. Depositor name for the register need not be true. Hesk waits fifty paces behind outside. Let the boy go.

DEPOSIT: Sebak left at the Lamplight Street counting-house, under the register name CROW, paper No. 417, one jot a night (paid for Wednesday night): (1) Bram's strongbox (sealed, locked, six stones inside), (2) the canvas satchel with the six pale bars in wool, (3) a canvas pouch containing the iron key, sealed with a blank grey disc. Sebak kept Bram's note for Rennick, Voss's signed note, and Voss's receipt. The house will hold them unopened; only the bearer of paper 417 may take them out. Hesk waits fifty paces off. Sebak's next move: Gilder's Row (unscouted).

RENNICK (Thomas? 'T. Rennick', Factor: Metals, Wire & Cloth; No. 9 Gilder's Row; fifties, thin, grey at the temples, ink on cuff; steward with drooping moustache). Insight 21: his fear is real and for himself; he has lost money on earlier shipments that never arrived and does not know why; he does NOT know who the man in grey is; he is HIDING the name of the person he buys for (a University connection, hand tightened on the note when University was mentioned). Rennick asked: is the box safe, and has it been opened? Truth: the box was opened, the seal lifted whole and replaced, hair broken, stones swapped for the bars; the box is in the vault under CROW paper 417. Sebak has not answered yet. Hesk outside.

RENNICK CAUGHT THE HEDGE (Deception 3 vs Insight 16): he knows Sebak is being careful with his words about whether the box was opened. He will not accuse but demands the truth: 'If you tell me plainly what you have done, I may be angry; I will not be surprised, and I may still pay the tinker his balance. If you do not, I will find out when I open it, and then I will not pay anyone anything.' Sebak must answer. Voss's note is on Rennick's desk.

RENNICK TOLD (trade): his client is a journeyman of the ARTIFICERY, WARRICK (she), who works on sympathy lamps and cold-iron locks for the Arcanum's great-house customers. The metal is NIGHTSILVER (old books): carries a sympathetic link with almost no loss; a hand-length bar holds an alar that would burn through steel. It comes from the north in small lots. Rennick has bought it 14 months through ONE supplier: 12 boxes, 9 whole, 3 lost (twice the carrier was found dead in a ditch); each time he had paid half in advance. He suspects the supplier robs his own carriers to sell twice. The supplier writes in a small hand, signs with a square, collects replies from a CHANDLER ON CANDLE ROW; Rennick has never seen him. Rennick now demands the truth about the box. Sebak has not answered.

SEBAK CONFESSED to Rennick: seal intact, bars secured elsewhere, stones in the box, ledger and letters untouched. Rennick: 'I do not forgive the lie but I understand it' (the stones decoy was sensible). He demands to see all six bars, the seal, the ledger and the letters and count them himself; if as said he will pay Bram's balance of 1.5 talents to Sebak and tell nobody about the stones. He is putting on a grey coat to go now with his steward. Sebak has not yet named the counting-house.

MEETING SET: Sebak refused to hand the nightsilver to Rennick; offered to speak well of Rennick and meet his contact. Rennick: the bars are Warrick's (she paid half in advance, three talents from her purse and a loan she can't afford). He sent his steward with a note; Warrick will receive Sebak TOMORROW (Thursday) AT NOON at the north end of the STONEBRIDGE, in the public gardens, with Rennick present; Sebak to bring ONE bar for Rennick to see. Bram's balance (1.5 talents) is payable only once Warrick has the bars in hand and is satisfied. Rennick declines coin from Sebak; he is owed a favour. The barge job is Thursday too (the Wren; time clash: the barge leaves Thursday; noon meeting may conflict).

XP LEDGER (house rule: mixed XP for meaningful things; level 2 at 300). Awarded so far: Felled Oak ambush 100; saved Bram (Medicine, moving him, getting him treated) 25; talking Voss into rehabilitation for Pell and arresting Calder 50; the night fight in the loft 50; striking the deal with Rennick and the Warrick meeting 50. TOTAL 275 / 300 (25 short of level 2). Site thread has been asked for a sheet XP bar; XP is not yet stored in state.json.

ARTIFICERY ('the Fishery'): long low dark-stone building behind the clock tower past the stables, seven tall chimneys (three smoking), front door with a porter's lodge (heavy man in a leather apron checking names against a ledger), side yard with a covered loading dock (copper and glass crates), smaller student door at the back. Hesk stopped at the south end of the bridge (watch has no authority across the river). A MAN IN A LONG GREY COAT leans against a wall across the lane from the loading dock, pretending to read a folded paper; he may be the same man who paid the boy; he is watching the yard. Sebak has not yet been noticed (unknown); Warrick not yet found.

THE WATCHER: Sebak's Perception 15 vs DC 12 gets a face: thin, mid-thirties, narrow pale clean-shaven face, dark hair under a wide grey hat, gloved hands. Has not noticed Sebak (unresolved). He is probably the grey man or his agent; he is watching Warrick's loading yard.

ASHDOWN (the man in grey; gives the name 'Ashdown', surely false; soft dry clerk's voice, smells of lavender and cold stone, grey eyes, unafraid). He knows Sebak went to Gilder's Row, left a box at the Cealdish house and has the bars somewhere. He CLAIMS the bars are his; says Rennick pays half in advance and then arranges for the carriers to be robbed so he need not pay the rest (three times, four with Sebak), and denies killing carriers ('they are hard to replace'). This is a mirror of Rennick's story: each blames the other. Truth undecided. The porter in the leather apron has noticed the two of them. Ashdown asked what Sebak wants for the bars. Sebak's Deception 19 let him approach unremarked. The bolas is still hidden under Sebak's cloak. Insight on Ashdown at the lane: Sebak 5+1=6 vs his Deception 9+6=15, Sebak read nothing. Ashdown asked what Sebak would take for the bars; awaiting answer. Ashdown's terms: Sebak gets one bar plus one hour of instruction (handling nightsilver) if he brings all the bars and tells all he knows about Rennick's door and the attackers. Meet: chandler with the green door, Candle Row, an hour after sundown Thursday (tomorrow). Ashdown offered the drawn square signature and Candle Row chandler as proof he is the supplier; he refused to say whether he is a sympathist. Ashdown named a hatter on Cobbler's Lane when asked about his hat (hat est. 4 jots). Conflict: Thursday noon Warrick meeting at the Stonebridge gardens; Thursday barge job. Lodging: Widow Hesper Dunn's back room over the stable, 6 drabs a night, paid for tonight (Wed). Cost of lodging is GM-only. Evening Wed: Sebak practised alar with the iron nails (adv 1/14, +6 = 20 vs DC 11). Slept uninterrupted over the stable; long rest taken, chakra 3/3, hit die regained. Today is Thursday: Warrick at noon at the Stonebridge gardens, the Wren barge job, and Ashdown at the Candle Row chandler an hour after sundown. Candle Row scouting (Perception 19+3=22): chandler Aldous Penn, green door; lavender-scented candles in the window; a small drawn square scratched low on the doorframe; a brass letter slot with a fresh grey envelope showing. Penn is a friendly, nervous man; GM to decide what he knows (he forwards letters for a customer who calls himself Ashdown). Insight on Penn: Sebak 17+1=18 (success). Penn is honestly terrified, not lying. He does not know the gentleman's real name; thin, soft-spoken, grey coat, pays a silver jot a month for the holding, collects at dusk. Two weeks ago a rough man with a scar on his cheek (Verrin) drew the square and demanded the post; Penn refused and he left cursing. Persuasion on Penn to hand over the post: d20 9 -1 = 8 vs DC 14, failed. Penn refused, but will pass on any message Sebak leaves; he will also tell the grey gentleman at dusk that a stranger drew the square (he is too afraid not to). Body Flicker out of Penn's shop (window view of the step) beside the sweeping boy; grapple Athletics 8+0 = 8 vs boy 12+1 = 13, failed. The boy dropped the broom and bolted down the alley behind the tallow works toward the river. Unknown whether he is a lookout or just frightened. Penn will have heard the commotion. Bolas thrown at the fleeing boy: Sebak ran 20 ft to get within 10 ft, attack d20 16+3 = 19 vs AC 12, hit; the boy is restrained and tangled (DC 11 Str to free himself). Bolas (2 kunai tied) are on the boy; recover them after. The boy is Tam, about eleven. A grey gentleman pays him 2 drabs a day to sweep Penn's step and watch who draws the square or asks after the post. If anyone does, Tam is to run and tell Gorrow, the chestnut seller at the south end of the Stonebridge, who passes it on. Tam has never seen the gentleman's face under the hat. He mentioned that the scarred man was seen too and that Tam was told to keep away from him. Tam's extra information: the grey gentleman collects the post at dusk and then walks down to the river stairs behind the tallow works, where a skiff waits. Yesterday morning (before Sebak met Ashdown) the gentleman gave Tam an extra silver jot and told him to watch for a young man in a dark vest with a short sword, who might come with a bandaged friend. So the gentleman was expecting Sebak before the lane encounter. Tam believes the gentleman is called 'Mister Ash' because Gorrow once said it. Ashdown is not the unknown; likely he is the grey man. XP ledger: 275 -> 285 (+10 for tracing Ashdown's watcher chain: Penn, Tam, Gorrow). Tam freed and bolas recovered; Tam agreed to say he got away. Tam may be useful later. Watching Gorrow: Stealth d20 2+7 = 9 vs his passive 11, spotted. Perception 16+3 = 19: Sebak sees Gorrow slip a folded scrap to a girl with a basket who then hurries into the market. Gorrow has recognised the dark vest and wakizashi from the gentleman's description. He is packing his brazier slowly. Gorrow is stocky, middle-aged, one-eyed. Tailing the basket girl: Stealth d20 1+7 = 8, failed. She noticed him at the second corner, shouted that a man was following her; the crowd and a fishwife blocked Sebak and she vanished into the market. Her scrap still unread. Gorrow's brazier is now gone from the bridge end. Sebak left word with Penn: 'I will keep the appointment at the green door after sundown.' Penn will pass it on to the grey man if he comes. Sebak paid the counting house 1 jot for Thursday night and withdrew one bar against paper No. 417; five bars remain in the vault. Arrived at the Stonebridge gardens at noon; Rennick is waiting on a bench, nervous. Perception at the gardens 6+3 = 9: Sebak sees no grey coat or wide grey hat. (GM: Ashdown is not on the terrace; a figure in grey may watch from the bridge later.) Warrick (woman, ~30, lean, pale eyes) says she wants nightsilver for locks/lamps with no link slippage; admitted when pressed: a perfected lock would free her from a debt to the Artificery and from her master (Master Orrel, the Fishery). She suspects someone inside the Artificery knows her business and is stealing the boxes, perhaps her master or a rival journeyman. Sebak handed the bar to Warrick under the yew; she shaved a sliver and burned it in a candle flame; flared white, genuine. She will pay Bram's 1.5 talents once all five remaining bars reach her (she wants them by tomorrow). The white flash was seen by Hesk at the gate and possibly by the gardener. Warrick/Rennick on history: 12 boxes in 14 months, but only 5 held nightsilver. The first nightsilver box (spring, two small bars) arrived safely; the next three were taken; this one (six bars) is the fifth. All three lost boxes were nightsilver; the first nine boxes were plain metals and never touched. Perception on Rennick 14+3 = 17: faint lavender scent on his coat collar and a fresh grey thread on his cuff; he never meets Warrick eyes when she talks of a leak; his right hand keeps patting an inner pocket (holds a folded letter with a drawn square signature). GM: he met the grey man in the last two days. Persuasion to dismiss Warrick and delay the other bars: d20 9-1 = 8 vs DC 10, failed. She demanded a fixed deadline: tomorrow (Friday) noon at the same bench, all five bars; otherwise she holds Bram's wage and tells Master Orrel of the delay. Pickpocket on Rennick: Sleight of Hand d20 4+5 = 9 vs passive 11, failed. He caught Sebak's wrist, white-faced and quiet. Hesk has drifted nearer. Rennick's trust in Sebak is damaged (he now suspects Sebak wants the letter). Rennick explained: he never robbed anyone; but for every nightsilver box he sent the route and day to the supplier via the Candle Row chandler, because the supplier said he would arrange guards (none ever came). He now fears his own letters leaked the routes. The pocket letter arrived at dawn by a boy, signed with a drawn square: Give the journeywoman one bar, tell her the rest follows, say nothing to her of me, and bring the courier to the green door on Candle Row at dusk Thursday. Rennick showed it to Sebak. Contradiction for Sebak: Ashdown (the supplier) claims Rennick arranges the robberies, but the supplier received every route. Sebak returned the letter to Rennick and let him go. Hesk trails Sebak at a distance (Voss is curious). Dusk meeting at the green door; the five bars are still in the counting-house vault. Sebak collected the strongbox and the satchel of five bars from the counting house (clerk Ostrel) against paper No. 417; the iron key and pouch stay in the vault. Hesk is across the street watching him carry the box. Hesk followed Sebak to Candle Row and loiters at the lane mouth. Penn's shop is open again; Tam is back sweeping the step and has noticed Sebak. Inside Penn's: Penn says the grey gentleman came at noon, unscheduled, took the grey envelope and left word (Penn passed on Sebak's yes): Sebak may wait in the back room until dusk; the gentleman will come through the river door. Penn knows nothing more. The back room has a river door, a table, a lamp and a stair. Sebak shaved a sliver from a bar with a kunai, and set a binding between it and the five bars: Consanguinity (piece to whole) = Perfect link, DC 8; Alar d20 19 (adv, 19/5) + 6 = 25, margin 17, almost no slippage, source his body heat. It lets him feel the bars' motion and direction. Occupies his one mental split; Body Flicker unavailable while held. Waiting: Perception 13+3 = 16. At dusk Sebak hears a skiff bump the river stairs, one set of soft boots on the stairs, and a second man staying in the skiff (cough, shifting weight; this is a poleman, not Verrin). Ashdown lifts the bar from the river door and enters alone, lavender, no hat brim low. Ashdown admits he told Rennick to give Warrick one bar as bait; he watched the gardens at noon (from the bridge) and says a master in a black Artificery gown (heavyset, white beard) watched the exchange from the bridge and left by the Fishery path afterwards; Ashdown implies this is Master Orrel. Unverified. Correction: Sebak handed the satchel of five bars to Ashdown, who counted them and gave Sebak a sixth bar from his coat as payment (not one of the five). The shaving still tracks the five. Ashdown offers the hour of instruction now or another evening. Sebak asked whether the bars reach Warrick tomorrow. Sebak called Ashdown back about the morning visit to Candle Row. Ashdown admits he has watchers (Penn, Tam, Gorrow) and knows about the square, the boy and the girl in the market; says Tam claimed to have slipped away at the river and he lets that stand. Ashdown calls it prudent, not hostile, and asks that Sebak not harm his boy. Friday morning: Sebak slept in the stable room (6 drabs paid), long rest, chakra 3/3, the tracking binding held through sleep. Overnight the bars moved by river then stopped across the water, east, near the Artificery side warehouses. Bram is 9/11. Warrick expects the five bars at noon at the gardens; Sebak does not hold them. Friday noon at the gardens: Warrick waiting on the same bench; Rennick absent. Passive Perception 13: a heavyset white-bearded man in a black gown stands at the bridge parapet watching (Master Orrel, unconfirmed). Hesk is at the south gate again. Persuasion to Warrick (honest delay, no names): d20 5-1 = 4 vs DC 13, failed. She does not trust it. She sets a new limit: tomorrow (Saturday) at noon at the same bench, or she tells Master Orrel the delay is Sebak's fault and asks the Arcanum wardens to look for him. The bearded man at the parapet turns away when she looks at him; GM: he is Orrel and heard enough. The binding leads to a tall shuttered net-loft on Wharf Lane, east bank, about three streets from the Artificery loading dock. Perception d20 2+3 = 5: Sebak noticed nothing but the padlocked door and a barrel by it. Stealth 8+7 = 15: unseen. GM: the loft is Ashdown's store; a poleman is dozing inside the skiff moored at the stairs behind (not seen). The five bars are inside. Sebak watched from the cooper's yard from early afternoon (Stealth 18+7 = 25, unseen). Quiet all afternoon. At dusk (Perception 11+3 = 14) the Artificery loading-dock porter arrived with a handcart and a hooded man (stocky, gloved), unlocked the padlock with a key from his belt, and carried out the satchel (canvas-wrapped) and loaded it under sacks. The binding tugs: the bars are moving. They set off toward the Artificery. The hooded man's face was not seen. Tailed the cart (Stealth 17+7 = 24, unseen). It went to a postern in the Artificery wall beside the loading dock. When the postern opened the lantern showed the hooded man push back his hood: Master Orrel, heavyset, white beard (passive Perception 13). Orrel and the porter carried the satchel inside; the postern was barred. The five bars are now inside the Artificery. GM: either Ashdown and Orrel are partners, or Orrel (via the porter) robbed Ashdown's cache; the porter had a key. Sebak practised in the copse for two hours: kunai throws 11, 22, 22 (+5), bolas throws 4 and 4 (nat 1s, tangled in a branch twice). No mechanical gain. The binding still holds and the bars are still in the Artificery. Deadline: Warrick at noon tomorrow. Bolas practice, six more throws (3,3,2,11,2,17 +3 = 6,6,5,14,5,20 vs a knot AC 10): the last throw wrapped the knot cleanly. Ruling: Sebak re-measured the twine and rebalanced the weights; bolas range now 15/30 ft. Still no proficiency. Sebak told Ashdown he watched the net-loft and saw the Artificery porter and Orrel (hooded then bared) take the satchel into the Artificery postern. Ashdown did NOT know: GM truth, Orrel robbed Ashdown with a copied key from the porter; Ashdown names only himself, Gorrow and the porter-cousin as key holders (the porter is Penn's cousin, Dobb). Ashdown's tell: very still, then cold. He offers a plan: retrieve the bars from the Artificery tonight or tomorrow, before Warrick's noon deadline; wants Sebak to enter. Sebak did not mention the binding. Ashdown agreed with Sebak: stealing the bars back only returns them to Orrel via Warrick (journeyman work belongs to the master by indenture). His better plan: expose Orrel. Under guild law a master who takes a journeyman's goods forfeits her indenture; if the guild wardens find the five bars in Orrel's workshop (Warrick supplies the complaint), Warrick is freed. Ashdown cannot appear publicly; Sebak would be the front. Needs Warrick at noon tomorrow. XP ledger: 285 -> 300 (+15 for the lesson with Ashdown). 300 reached: level 2 ready; ask the player when to level up. Lesson content: Ashdown noticed the held tracking binding at once (he is a sympathist, trained; he named it unprompted). He taught Sebak to slacken the thread (a taut binding can be felt by another sympathist at its anchor; Orrel may have trained sympathists in the Artificery) and to use two sympathies of similar mass (counterweight) to reduce slippage on poor links by one tier once per day in GM discretion. He would not say where he trained. Sebak is exhausted but eager. LEVEL UP to 2 (xp 300): Rogue 2. HP max 10 -> 17 (hit die roll 2, took the average 5, +2 CON = 7). Hit dice 2/2. Gained Cunning Action. Proficiency stays +2. No new chakra max. Player chose Counterweight at level 2 (kept HP 17). Cunning Action stays as the Rogue 2 class feature; the player noted Body Flicker already disengages. Cunning Action removed at the player request and folded into Improved Flicker. Saturday: Sebak slept in the stable room (6 drabs), long rest, chakra 3/3, HP 17/17. Plan with Ashdown: persuade Warrick to file a complaint with the Arcanum wardens against Orrel so the wardens find the five bars in his workshop. Bars still inside the Artificery. Binding slackened per the lesson. Persuasion to Warrick about Orrel: d20 4-1 = 3, failed. She does not believe a stranger accusing her master, but she will look herself: Orrel is at the guild hall until four; she holds a workshop key. She will go in alone at three; if she finds the bars she will file the complaint, if not she names Sebak to the wardens. Sebak told her about the supplier only as the seller, no name. Hat from Meris: she asked 5 jots, Persuasion d20 15-1 = 14 vs DC 12 haggled to 4 jots. Hat is flavour only. Fishery gate with Warrick at three. Hat dyed black and embroidered with the Uchiha fan by Meris for 3 jots; ready by two. Cealdish locals read it as a foreign house badge; only those who know the Uchiha could recognise it. Correction: Meris charged 1 jot 5 drabs, not 3 jots, for the dye and fan stitching (player rightly objected that it was dearer than the hat). Warrick went into the Artificery at three. Twenty minutes later she came out pale: the five bars are in Orrel locked cabinet in his workshop; she did not touch them. She will go to the wardens. Orrel came back early from the guild hall with two apprentices (sympathists, grey cuffs) and stopped her at the gate; Dobb the porter hovers. Orrel is genial and heavy, watching Sebak. The binding is slack but Orrel apprentices may sense it. Insight on Orrel: Sebak 16+1 = 17 vs Orrel Deception 20+4 = 24 (nat 20): read nothing, he looks genuinely fatherly and concerned. Orrel asked Sebak his name, noted the crest on the hat as foreign, and told the two apprentices (Pell and Vane) to wait by the gatehouse. Sebak lied: Warrick pet hamster died and he had just told her. Deception d20 17-1 = 16 vs Orrel Insight 14+3 = 17: Orrel is not fooled but plays along; he said he believed Warrick kept a linnet, then accepted her nod. He is now alert; apprentices Pell and Vane drift closer. Warrick improvised well. Sebak walked with Orrel into the yard. Orrel probed gently; then told Sebak his apprentices felt a thread today, a very fine one, running from outside the wall to his own cabinet (the binding, even slack). He asks if Sebak knows anything about it. The yard has the gate behind them, the apprentices two paces back, Dobb at the gate, the long workshop ahead. Sebak claimed to be from the Academy and said Orrel has the bars but he has no jurisdiction to enter; if Orrel carries them out they are fair game to be confiscated. Deception with disadvantage (no seal, foreign badge, no gown): d20 10,9 -> 9-1 = 8 vs Orrel Insight 20+3 = 23. Failed badly. Orrel is calm, not fooled; asks for the commission and which master signed it. Apprentices behind Sebak. Dobb is closing the gate with Warrick on the street side. Sebak doubled down: an unofficial secret operative. Orrel does not believe it; he reframes Sebak as an unaccredited intruder who has bound a thread to his cabinet and ordered Pell and Vane to hold him and Dobb to fetch the town watch. Hesk is the only watchman nearby and is not under Orrel control. Pell and Vane are young sympathists (AC 11, 8 HP each, daggers, can bind). No combat yet. Sebak let the apprentices hold him. Dobb brought Hesk and two watchmen (Tolly and Brack). Orrel accused Sebak of trespass and of binding a thread to his cabinet, and demanded a search for stolen goods. Hesk is Voss man and recognises Sebak; he asked Sebak to turn out his cloak. Sebak carries one nightsilver bar (Ashdown payment) and the sliver. Warrick stands outside the gate. Sebak used Improved Flicker (1 chakra, 2/3 left) to escape the apprentices grip and land outside the iron gate beside Warrick. Correction: maintaining a binding does NOT block Flicker; it only occupies the mental split, and the bonus action is shared. Sebak claimed the bars were once his and somehow ended in Orrel cabinet, with Warrick to testify. Warrick backs him: saw five bars in a canvas satchel in Orrel locked cabinet. Hesk will take everyone to the Arcanum wardens, and posts watchman Tolly at the workshop door so no one touches the cabinet. Orrel protests, composed. Sebak waited in the wardens antechamber across the Stonebridge while Warrick swore her complaint before Warden Maren Isk (middle-aged, grey gown, white seal, a trained sympathist). At dusk the wardens returned with Warrick, Sebak, Hesk and Orrel to the workshop. Tolly kept the door. The cabinet, opened by Orrel with his own key, holds only lamps and wire. The binding still pulls, steady, from the room: the bars are somewhere in the building. Sebak suggested Warden Isk look where the pull led. She followed it (her own trained sense), to the cold crucible furnace at the left of the cabinet: under a layer of cinders in the ash pan, the canvas satchel with five bars. Orrel was visibly stunned and said the porter Dobb must have done it; Dobb slipped away during the search (not found). Wardens confiscated the bars pending inquiry; Orrel is suspended from guild duties pending a hearing; Warrick indenture is under review by the wardens. GM truth: Orrel did take the bars; Dobb hid them at Orrel signal during the quarter hour and has bolted. Ashdown and the supplier owe the bars to the wardens now. XP ledger 300 -> 325 (+25 for exposing Orrel). Warden Isk wants to speak with Sebak and Warrick tomorrow at the hall. After the search: Warden Isk wants Sebak and Warrick at the hall tomorrow morning. Warrick thanked Sebak, cannot pay Bram until the wardens release the bars (hearing within the week), promised she would; asked Sebak to stay for the hearing. Hesk told Sebak Voss expects an account and a drink. Ashdown still expects word at the chandler after dusk tonight. Sebak told Ashdown the outcome: Orrel exposed, five bars seized by the wardens, hearing within the week, Dobb fled. Ashdown cold-satisfied; says he will not claim the bars publicly (he cannot give his name). Penn then confessed Dobb knocked at the back door an hour ago, white-faced, and Penn hid him in the cellar. Ashdown proposes they go down and ask Dobb what Orrel paid him. XP ledger 325 -> 340 (+15, Dobb confession). Dobb confession in Penn's cellar: he read Penn's post when he visited and sold the routes to Orrel (a steward gave him the purse; Orrel himself told him to copy Ashdown's loft key and to hide the satchel in the furnace at a signal when the watch came). Orrel hired the robbers: Verrin, Calder Marsh, Garrick Finch, Pell; the two dead carriers were Verrin work, not Orrel orders. Orrel wanted the nightsilver because the guild charter bans journeymen from working it unreported and he wanted to claim Warrick lock for himself. Dobb will testify to Warden Isk if protected. Agreed: Penn shelters Dobb tonight; Ashdown and Sebak bring him to the hall at first bell. Verrin is still loose, unpaid. Sebak resolves to join the University (Academy). Funds 1t 7j 4d plus one bar (Ashdown). Tuition 2-3 talents plus term room ~1 talent, set at interview, no referral needed. Warden Isk, Warrick or Ashdown could speak for him. Ashdown taught how to use nightsilver: (1) as a relay, place a sliver in a chain of two links and the slippage of each drops a tier at the GM discretion; (2) as a store, it absorbs heat, motion or chakra slowly and gives it back in a rush (lamps, locks, flares); (3) never heat it fast, it flares white and blinds within 10 ft (CON save DC 12 or blinded 1 round). Ashdown agreed Sebak may contact him through Penn (a drawn square on a folded note) and may source more nightsilver in future, but not quickly or cheaply: his source is slow, the road is dangerous while Verrin is loose, and each bar costs him dearly. He asks Sebak never to give his name to the Academy. Price/terms are GM-only and set later. Sebak long-rested (chakra 3/3). Bram healed to 11/11 over the night. Farewells to Bram and Marta done at dawn Sunday; Bram still owed 1.5 talents (from Warrick once bars released). Sebak now at Penn's shop with Ashdown and Dobb for the walk to the wardens' hall at first bell. XP ledger 340 -> 360 (+20: testimony brought to the wardens, account given). Isk took Dobb into protective custody, issued a summons for Orrel, and sent wardens after Verrin, Marsh, Finch (Pell already known). Warrick's indenture review set for the hearing. Isk will write Sebak a short letter of character for the University interview (he must collect it before leaving; it is sealed with the white seal). Ashdown waits outside; he does not enter the hall. Sebak left Imre for the University on foot, Sunday mid-morning. Ashdown parted with a nod and his warning to keep his name from the Academy. Tamsin: 18-ish applicant from a farming town, poor, over-talkative, wants an escort; his mule Biscuit has a swollen left fore fetlock (Sebak rebound it, rest needed). Sebak intends to part ways at the gates. Dice: Animal Handling nat 1 first try, then 10 with advantage. Ferry-Pole inn: Sebak paid 1 jot 5 drabs (bed, supper, stabling for Biscuit); Tamsin paid his own share. Currency now 1 talent 5 jots 9 drabs. GM truth: the drover's grey men are Marsh (limp), Finch (crossbow) and a silent third, Orrel's hirelings fleeing east after the wardens moved on Imre; they robbed the drover at a bend east of the Ferry-Pole. The University man in the grey cloak is Master Corwin's scribe, Hale (see Corwin Hale lead): sharper than he looks, reading the room; Sebak insight roll 2 failed. Insight rolls: drover 15, scribe 2.

player_notes.title: The delivery (done)
player_notes.text: Bram's strongbox went to Rennick of Gilder's Row, who buys nightsilver for Warrick, a journeywoman of the Artificery. I gave Warrick one bar at the Stonebridge gardens. Master Orrel, her master, stole the other five through the porter Dobb. I traced them to the Artificery, and Warden Maren Isk found them in Orrel's cold furnace. Orrel is suspended and the wardens hold the bars. Bram's wage of 1.5 talents is due from Warrick once the bars are released.

player_notes.title: Open threads
player_notes.text: Verrin, the scar-faced crossbowman who hired the robbers and killed two carriers, is still loose. Dobb is hiding at Penn's and will testify at first bell at the wardens' hall (west bank, white seal over the door). Warden Isk wants my account. The Salt Barrel's barman slipped away. Marta wants a sliver of nightsilver for a test. Voss expects an account and a drink. Pell was to point out the heavy brigand at the Salt Barrel; his hearing is still pending.

player_notes.title: Ashdown
player_notes.text: Thin, pale, soft-spoken, long grey coat, wide hat, smells of lavender. Calls himself Ashdown. Signs with a drawn square. He says he is the nightsilver supplier. He taught me an hour of binding, gave me a bar, and told me what nightsilver does. Contact him through Penn, the chandler with the green door on Candle Row, with a folded note marked with a drawn square. I promised never to give his name to the Academy. He would not say if he is a sympathist; he plainly is.

player_notes.title: Who is who
player_notes.text: Bram: tinker from Crosson, recovering at Marta's. Marta: the apothecary. Sergeant Voss: south gate watch; Hesk is his plain-clothes man. Rennick: factor in metals, Gilder's Row. Warrick: journeywoman. Orrel: her master, now suspended. Dobb: Penn's cousin and the Artificery porter. Penn: chandler. Tam: the boy on his step. Gorrow: the chestnut seller who passes messages. Warden Maren Isk: grey gown, white seal, a trained sympathist.

player_notes.title: Nightsilver: what I know
player_notes.text: A pale, heavy metal. It relays a binding with almost no slippage, so a sliver in a chain drops each link a tier. It stores heat, motion or chakra and gives it back in a rush. Never heat it fast: it flares white and blinds. I keep one bar. My shaving is still bound to the five bars the wardens hold.

player_notes.title: Seeking out at the Academy
player_notes.text: Ashdown's advice: Master Kilvin of the Artificery (plain, soot to the elbows, respects honest craft), Master Lorren of the Archives (careful, slow), and Master Elodin, who teaches names. Marta also mentioned Corwin Hale of the Medica. I intend to apply to the University. No referral is needed.

player_notes.title: Warden Isk
player_notes.text: Woman with a tight pinned braid, grey gown, white seal; she runs the inquiry into Orrel and the bars. Took Dobb's testimony and my account. Promised a sealed letter of character for the University.
